business_problem: Alsemy needed to replace slow, expert-only semiconductor device-modeling workflows that required months or years of manual physics fitting before chip teams could move on new process nodes.
solution_summary: Alsemy rebuilt semiconductor device modeling around physics-informed AI so customers no longer have to wait months or years for experts to hand-fit SPICE and T-CAD models. Its Alsis platform learns transistor behavior directly from I-V and C-V datasets, while Alsphere extends the approach to structural and process modeling, including a display-focused variant co-developed with LG Display. Model development runs on NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPUs with NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo and CUDA-accelerated PyTorch across a hybrid on-premises and cloud environment, letting a small team iterate quickly on pretrained Retarget and C-V models. Once trained, the models can be fine-tuned with customer data and then deployed for CPU-based inference inside customer environments, so fabs keep sensitive data on-premises while still benefiting from GPU-accelerated training and rapid experimentation.

data_flow: I-V and C-V measurements plus real silicon data feed PhysicsNeMo and PyTorch training on RTX GPUs, pretrained and customer-specific models are refined in Alsis and Alsphere, and the resulting models are delivered for CPU-based inference inside customer R&D and fab environments.
business_outcome: Alsemy cut device-modeling cycles from years of physics work and months of manual fitting to weeks of GPU training, one-second inference, and 10-minute customer tuning, helping semiconductor R&D teams move faster with lower cost and expert-level accuracy.
